newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gold Fields upbeat on Ghana surface mining.
newsitem.headline: Gold Fields upbeat on Ghana surface mining.

text.p: Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd was upbeat on Wednesday that its plans for open cast mining at Tarkwa in south-west Ghana would be in the black within six years.
"Six years from now we will be in a positive cash flow and will be paying tax," Richard Robinson, Gold Fields' executive director for new business, told a news briefing.
Tarkwa is run by Gold Fields Ghana, in which GFSA holds 70 percent, and Robinson said the exploration venture would net GFSA handsome profits.

Ghana's government, he estimated, would net $500 million from the mining venture over 20 years if the gold price averaged $390 over the period. GFSA's earnings would be considerably less due to taxation because it only has a two-year tax shield.
Robinson said initial capital costs would total around $125 million excluding contingencies which Gold Fields and the other stakeholders would fund through shareholder loans.
Gold Fields was not keen to list its Ghana operations and felt its shareholders would be very disappointed if this became necessary to meet the costs in subsequent phases, he said.
"Standing here now I have no wish to list," Robinson said, adding however this might be reassessed when the third phase started with the construction of the first carbon-in-pulp plant.
Production costs at Tarkwa are in the region of $210 an ounce. Proven reserves are 13 million ounces, and the average grade is 1.4 grams a tonne.
The first gold pour is expected in about a year with production scheduled to build up from 100,000 ounces in 1988 to about 250,000 ounces by the year 2000.

The Tarkwa surface mining project is expected to secure the concession's future with the current underground mine showing markedly reduced profits for the second half of 1996. Net income dropped to $354,000 from $783,000 in the last half of 1995.

The Canadian-based Golden Knight Resources Inc also holds a 17.5 percent shareholding in Gold Fields Ghana, while the Ghana government has 10 percent and Ghana's Social Security and National Investment Trust 2.5 percent.
